title: Payments Operations Note: Returned Payments on Equipment & Vehicle Loans
content:
**Rule.** A payment on an Equipment & Vehicle Loans loan returned unpaid by the member's bank is reversed entry by entry: each interest and principal payment entry of the returned remittance gets its own return entry with the original amount and effective date, pointing to it, which reopens the installment it had paid. A payment may be reversed only once. One returned payment fee of the product's returned payment fee amount is assessed per returned remittance, booked from the principal return entry automatically (an interest-only remittance books the fee from its interest return entry in the same way), and no fee is charged when the return reason is unauthorized. A late charge that becomes due because the reopened installment is now late is assessed under the late-charge terms as of the day it arises.

## What a return produces

| Returned remittance | Return entries | Returned payment fee |
|---|---|---|
| Interest and principal payment entries | one return entry for each, same amount and effective date, each pointing to the entry it reverses | one fee for the remittance, booked from the principal return entry |
| Interest-only remittance | one return entry for the interest payment | one fee, booked from the interest return entry |
| Any remittance returned as unauthorized | return entries as above | none |

## Reversal only once

Whether a payment entry has already been reversed is read from the loan's records: a payment entry that already has a principal or interest return entry pointing to it is not reversed again.

## Hypothetical illustration

A remittance of 1800.00 paid an installment as 450.00 of interest and 1350.00 of principal and is returned for insufficient funds. Two return entries are booked — 450.00 against the interest payment and 1350.00 against the principal payment, each with the original effective date — and the installment reopens. One returned payment fee is assessed for the remittance (30.00 on every product of the line). Had the bank returned the same remittance as unauthorized, the two return entries would be booked and no fee charged.
